- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is rising, cap the increase at 2–3% above recent mean to avoid false optimism.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, apply a slight downward bias (−1–2%) to account for mean reversion.  
- If forecast overshoots true outcome by >5% in 3–5 consecutive days, reduce subsequent forecast by 1–2% per day to correct for lagged momentum.  
- When sentiment is volatile (fluctuating >0.35) and forecast is smooth, introduce a 1–2% smoothing penalty to avoid overfitting to recent trends.  
- For forecasts with high initial error (|forecast - true| > 3%), adjust by averaging the last 3–5 true values before the forecast horizon to anchor to reality.
